title: LDAP.main and LDAP.spare
summary: Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25: wherever LDAP main and LDAP hot spare are this minute, they are LDAP.main and LDAP.spare; when LDAP.main goes down LDAP.spare becomes LDAP.main. These are service addresses kept on separate sites, not addresses of nodes that may vanish when someone pulls a power plug. RolePair keeps a main and a spare on separate sites with fabric state. muDown(mu) (quorum decided): FENCE_ROLE raises the role epoch so the old main is refused if it returns; ROUTE_SERVICE moves .main to the spare; a new spare is activated on a site other than the new main, checked (replica generation) and only then routed as .spare. No other site: reported, never hidden. Failover steps are pre-approved recovery (arbitrator.recovery). Open: LDAP.main route publication must not depend on the dead LDAP.main (override files or a direct daemon announce).
authority: built and tested offline (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-25)
invariants: Main and spare are on separate sites
The old main is fenced before .main moves
A new spare is named only after it has caught up
Running without a spare is reported
procedure: Decide how the LDAP.main route is published when LDAP.main itself has failed
